content:Speaker user says: What are some benefits of SMS marketing campaigns for subscribers?
Generate according to: Why would you sign up for an SMS marketing campaign? This is a good question to ask yourself as you develop your own text marketing program.
Texts give you access to customers — and they get exclusive access to you.
Although many consumers are open to receiving texts from businesses, at the end of the day they expect to get something of value for giving a business their phone numbers. Texts remain a disruptive avenue for communication. This makes customers much more picky about which companies they sign up for text alerts. Therefore, every message you send must have a purpose that responds to the wants and needs of your customers.
SMS marketing campaigns offer many benefits to subscribers. They can get offers and deals, the latest updates on your business, and more. One of the most important features to provide as part of your service is access, as in exclusive access.
You have potential multiple touch points with customers. Many of them see your advertisements, follow you on social media, receive your emails and perhaps still get your mailings. Therefore, you need to give them a reason to sign up for one more. Even customers who only follow you on one channel still need some motivation to add another one.
People have a special relationship with their cell phones. Most people do not wish to have their phone further than arm’s length at all times through the day. They are also more hesitant to give out their cell phone number than their email or social media information. Therefore, it provides an avenue for more intimate access.
People carry their phones with them everywhere so that they do not miss out.
Your messages will be delivered right next to messages that are mostly from friends and family members, especially as fewer marketers take advantage of the service compared to email and social media. This fosters a closer relationship between you and your customers.
With regular messages to your subscribers, you have the opportunity to further engage with customers and build an even stronger relationship. They are already interested enough to hear about your company that they handed over their cell phone number. Then, they will continue to get messages from you, reinforcing their interest in your company. By receiving messages, they also feel as though they are in a special group of your customers. This continues to build your relationship until they have become loyal customers.
It is common to set up some type of loyalty reward program to treat your regular customers. Rather than notifying these consumers through email or apps, try your SMS marketing program. A recent study found that 48 percent preferred texting as the means of communication, which was higher than email at 22 percent and apps at 20 percent. However, only a few marketers actually do this. The same study found that only 21 percent used texting for their loyalty program.
You do not want to miss out on a way to communicate with your most loyal customers. By sending messages in a way that they prefer, you continue to develop the relationship towards loyalty even more. This will increase your chances of conversions since you are sending messages to people who are already interested in your business in a way that they prefer. This deepens their positive feelings in association with your business, further enhancing their loyalty.
It is easy to set up your SMS marketing program to send out loyalty messages. You do not have to limit your access to other subscribers by doing so. Simply create multiple groups out of your subscriber list and send targeted messages based on people’s demographics, shopping patterns, loyalty status and other data.
Get your team together to build the best content possible.
When you build the content, not only do you want it to not replicate what you have sent out through other channels, but it also should not duplicate itself. Although you might have a few templates that you rotate for your messages, the actual content needs to be unique. You want to keep people seeing the value of remaining a subscriber so that you have the chance to continue to build your relationship.
Quality content also keeps people interested in remaining part of your program. This not only allows you to continue to provide them with exclusive access, but it also continues to provide you with access to engaged customers to drive business.

content:Speaker assistant says: Certainly! Here are some tips on how to create engaging content for your SMS marketing campaign:

1. Keep it short and sweet: Remember that SMS messages have a character limit, so make sure your message is concise and easy to understand.

2. Personalize your messages: Include the recipient's name in your message, and tailor your content based on their preferences and interests whenever possible. This will make your messages feel more personal and relevant to them.

3. Provide value: Make sure your messages provide something of value to the recipient, whether that's a special offer or discount, exclusive access to new products or information, or helpful tips and advice.

4. Use strong language: Choose powerful, action-oriented words that will grab the reader's attention and inspire them to take action.

5. Include a clear call-to-action: Make sure your message has a clear call-to-action, such as "Click this link to learn more" or "Reply with YES to receive your discount code."

6. Incorporate multimedia: Consider including images or videos in your messages to make them more visually appealing and engaging.

7. Test and optimize: Use A/B testing to see what types of messages and content resonate best with your audience, and continually refine your approach based on what works best.

By following these tips, you can create engaging and effective SMS marketing messages that will help you reach and engage with your audience effectively. context:This guide outlines seven specific strategies for creating concise, personalized, and effective SMS marketing campaigns that drive engagement and conversions. keywords: SMS marketing, engaging content, call-to-action, personalization, optimization, multimedia, short messages tags: concise_content_strategy, action_oriented_language, multimedia_integration, a_b_testing, personalization_tactics

content:Speaker assistant says: Here are some steps you can take to ensure your product pricing is competitive:

1. Identify your competitors: Start by identifying the companies that offer similar products or services to yours. Look for businesses that operate in the same industry, target the same customer segment, and have a similar business model.

2. Understand their pricing strategies: Once you've identified your competitors, research their pricing strategies. Look at their prices, discounts and offers, and try to understand why they have chosen a particular pricing approach.

3. Analyze their pricing structure: Look at your competitors' pricing structure to identify their most popular price points, product bundles, and discounts. This will help you gauge what customers are willing to pay and what they expect in return.

4. Benchmark your pricing: Use the information you have gathered to benchmark your pricing strategy against your competitors. If your prices are significantly higher or lower than your competitors' prices, you may want to adjust your strategy.

5. Set your pricing strategy: Based on your analysis, set your pricing strategy. Choose a pricing model that aligns with your customers' expectations, and consider how your pricing will affect your market positioning and profitability.

6. Monitor and adjust: Once you have set your pricing strategy, monitor your competitors closely and be ready to adjust your strategy as necessary. Keep an eye on market trends and shifts in customer needs, and adjust your pricing accordingly. context:This content outlines a six-step process for researching and adjusting business pricing to remain competitive against industry standards and gain a market advantage, while the new context integrates specific promotional tactics analysis. keywords: competitor analysis, pricing strategy, product pricing tags: pricing_strategy_advice, market_analysis_process, strategic_pricing_framework, industry_standards_compliance, promotional_tactics_inquiry, competitor_analysis, production_cost_analysis, value_based_pricing, market_segmentation

content:Speaker assistant says: Sure! Here are some pricing models you can choose from:

1. Cost-plus pricing: This involves calculating the total cost of producing a product and adding a markup to determine the selling price. This pricing model ensures that you cover your costs and make a profit. 2. Value-based pricing: This involves pricing your products based on the perceived value to your customers. You determine the price based on what your customers are willing to pay, not just the cost of production. 3. Competitive pricing: This involves pricing your products based on the prices of your competitors. You adjust your prices to match or beat your competitors' prices. 4. Dynamic pricing: This involves changing your prices based on changes in supply and demand. For example, you might offer discounts during off-peak seasons or when you have excess inventory. 5. Freemium pricing: This involves offering a basic version of your product or service for free, while charging for premium features or upgrades. 6. Subscription pricing: This involves charging customers a recurring fee for access to your products or services on an ongoing basis. 7. Bundled pricing: This involves offering multiple products or services together at a discounted price as a bundle. Remember, the right pricing model for your business will depend on various factors like the nature of your product or service, your target customer segment, and your business goals. context:This content outlines a six-step methodology for developing a comprehensive pricing strategy that balances production costs, market demand, and target audience needs to ensure profitability. keywords: pricing models, cost-plus pricing, value-based pricing tags: pricing_strategy_advice, market_analysis_process, strategic_pricing_framework, industry_standards_compliance, promotional_tactics_inquiry, cost_benefit_analysis, target_audience_pricing, production_cost_analysis, market_demand_analysis

content:Speaker assistant says: To create a comprehensive pricing strategy for your products, consider the following steps:

1. Determine your production costs: Calculate the costs of labor, materials, and overhead expenses to produce each unit of your product. This will give you a baseline for pricing.

2. Understand market demand: Conduct market research to understand what consumers are willing to pay for your product relative to similar offerings. This will help you set a price that is attractive to customers while still allowing you to make a profit.

3. Define your target audience: Consider the demographic, geographic, psychographic, and behavioral characteristics of your primary customer segments. This information will help you tailor your pricing strategy to meet the needs and preferences of your target audience.

4. Choose your pricing strategy: Select a pricing model that aligns with your business goals, market demand, and production costs. Popular pricing strategies include cost-plus pricing, value-based pricing, penetration pricing, and skimming pricing.

5. Decide on discounts and promotions: Offer discounts and promotions strategically to incentivize purchases, increase sales, and build customer loyalty. Consider offering quantity discounts, seasonal promotions, bundle discounts, and referral discounts.

6. Communicate your pricing strategy: Clearly communicate your pricing strategy to customers through your website, marketing materials, and sales channels. Ensure that your pricing is easy to understand and that customers feel confident in their purchasing decision.

By following these steps and regularly assessing your pricing strategy, you can ensure that your products are priced competitively while still providing a healthy profit margin. context:This content outlines a comprehensive pricing strategy framework that balances costs, market demand, and promotional tactics to align with business goals. keywords: pricing strategy, production costs, market demand tags: purchase_validation, research_importance, deal_seeking_behavior, research_strategies, purchase_validation, market_research_integration, market_demand_assessment, pricing_strategy_steps

content:Speaker user says: Here is a piece of text: It’s the most wonderful time of the year. I’m not talking about Christmas, although that’s pretty joyous, too.
December is also Grammy season in Lafayette and surrounding area. Musicians and fans anticipate Grammy nominations, released Dec. 7 , like kids spying to see if reindeer really know how to fly.
This season did not disappoint as three locals claimed Grammy nominations. I hesitate to call them local as all three have fans and footprints all over the country.
Lafayette native Lauren Daigle continues her rise to Christian music superstardom with two Grammy nominations. Daigle’s “Look Up Child” CD, which already has more than 16 million views on YouTube, is nominated for Best Contemporary Christian Music Album.
Daigle’s single, “You Say,” is a nominee for Best Contemporary Christian Music Performance/Song. Hometown fans lucky enough to get tickets can catch her “Behold Christmas Tour” Friday and Monday at the Heymann Performing Arts Center.
Sean Ardoin, a 49-year-old zydeco musician who’s been on stage for 38 years, also scored a double. Ardoin’s “Kreole Rock and Soul” CD earned a Best Regional Roots Music Album nomination. The single “Kicks Rocks” is up for Best American Roots Performance.
Ardoin’s heritage goes back to zydeco’s roots with his grandfather, Creole music great Alphonse “Bois Sec” Ardoin, and his grandfather’s legendary cousin, Amede Ardoin. He’s part of a fourth generation of Ardoin recording artists, which includes his brother Chris, leader of the popular Nu Step Zydeko band.
The song spent a whopping 32 weeks at No. 1 on Billboard’s Hot Gospel Song chart, a first for a female artist. Not bad for an artist who turns 21 on Dec. 26.
Winners will be announced Feb. 10 at the 61st Grammy Awards in Los Angeles.
I’m always cautious about picking winners. But chances are above average for this year’s hometown crop.
All have quality recordings. Frankly, name recognition goes a long way, which gives Daigle a huge boost. Lately, her name has been in music headlines and beyond almost every week.
Hawthorne is a young talent that people are still discovering. But a hit song at No. 1 for eight months speeds up that process.
But Ardoin’s playing field is much more level in Regional Roots. He competes with New Orleans funk and Mardi Gras Indians group Cha Wa, Hawaiian singers Na Hoa and Kalani Pe’a and Native American musicians Young Spirit.
History is on his side. A Louisiana artist has won Regional Roots Grammy six times since the category was created in 2012.
Congratulations to all the hometown artists, who can savor an early Christmas. Thousands of artists try, but only a handful get to wear the lifetime title – Grammy nominee.
Herman Fuselier is music and entertainment writer for the Times of Acadiana and the Daily Advertiser. Contact him at hfuselier@theadvertiser.com.

content:Speaker user says: Here is a piece of text: Heather Lyke may have the most difficult job in college athletics: She's charged with infusing passion into Eastern Michigan University's programs amid dismal interest in her football team and very public criticism about its costs.
Yet she's not playing defensively as she prepares her staff to lead teams into the fall.
When the Eagles open the season on Sept. 2 at home in Ypsilanti, fans will see new priority seating at the 50 yard line, a new Touchdown Terrace for casual game viewing with food and alcohol sales, and a new vision for alumni fund-raising.
Lyke also is working under a new budgeting system that administrators say will bring public transparency to processes. And she's finding ways to inspire the athletes on campus under her watch while looking for creative ways to attract fans to Rynearson Stadium.
"I'm undeterred," said Lyke during an interview in early July. "We have a phenomenal coaching staff. We're part of an amazing conference.
"... I believe in what we're doing."
EMU football recorded the lowest average football attendance in the U.S. Among Division I FBS schools last season, when the team's record was 1-11. It has struggled for many years, something that Lyke recognized when she was hired in July 2013.
She brought on new football coach Chris Creighton just a few months later, and speaks of her support for him, his recruits and his approach to cultivating a team.
She also comes to work daily knowing that administrators throughout EMU want to maintain the athletics at the Division I level. All of the EMU regents signed a letter of support for athletics, citing Lyke.
"She has assembled an outstanding support team and we already have seen positive results in terms of continuing Eastern's championship traditions in a number of our sports, as well as in many new initiatives to increase revenues," according to the April 26 open letter.
The regents distributed the reaction in late April following the most recent criticism from staff over the school's funding of athletics. It also followed airing of an HBO Real Sports documentary that was critical of school sports spending.
EMU's Interim President Donald Loppnow and President-Elect James Smith, as well as all eight of its Board of Regents members signed off on an open letter to the campus community, alumni, friends and supporters expressing support for the football program and its affiliation with the Mid-American Conference.
Records submitted by EMU to the NCAA indicate that EMU's athletic budget in 2015 was $33.9 million. Of that, $18.1 million was a direct subsidy by the school.
The show of support meant a lot to Lyke. It means there are no fissures among top leadership as she focuses on her role: Building champions, building the EMU brand and building e-commerce.
Lyke said she wants EMU's athletes on all 21 teams to feel that playing college sports is "one of the most remarkable experiences of their life." Yet one sport gets much of her focus.
"The reality is, we've got to focus on football," she said. "It's our most visible engine."
The coming season gives EMU six home games to expose students and the community to its team. In November, two games will be midweek instead of on Saturdays -- one way to stand out on a crowded football weekend.
Five games will be televised on ESPN networks, giving the Eagles what Lyke calls "tremendous exposure" -- and more TV revenue. That's up from three the previous year, and zero in 2013.
Seating inside the stadium adds new options. The premium seating will be found in eight outdoor groups of four seats in "loges." If all sell, it will generate $12,800.
More premium seating will be available at "Touchdown terrace," the large patio along the atrium of the Convocation Center.
"People love the view from here," Lyke said, as she pointed to the football field. Alcohol and food from new concession partner Chartwells will be sold, and it already boasts one client: The Alumni Association, which will be moving its pre-game event from a tent in the parking lot to the interior location.
All of that should help the team draw more fans. It also aids the revenue-building part of Lyke's job, she said. This year's budget didn't fill one position and calls for a $353,000 cut in operational costs. But additional efforts, like new marketing agreements through licensing partner IMG, are expected to add dollars to the program.
So are donations. Cash donations went up 45 percent in the year ended June 30, reaching almost $800,000 -- and setting a school record. The number of donors topped 1,300, a 21 percent increase.
All of the pieces should be in place to increase the measurable aspects of running the state's fourth-largest athletic program at a public university, she said. The intangibles are lining up, too, as she and coaches mentor athletes.
Their hopes are high for a good season, Lyke said. "We know what we need to do."
Eastern Michigan head coach Chris Creighton appeared optimistic Monday in a video sent out to alumni of the football program.
Heather Lyke has done well enough in her first two years as Eastern Michigan University's athletic director to earn two more.

content:Speaker assistant says: Step-by-Step Guide to Improve Event Planning Skills:

1. Assess Your Current Skills: Assess your current event planning skills to identify areas that need improvement. Focus on areas such as project management, budgeting, vendor management, creative problem solving, and communication skills.

2. Set Clear Goals: Once you have identified your areas of weakness, set clear goals for improving your skills in these areas. Create a timeline with specific milestones to measure your progress.

3. Attend Training Programs: There are several training programs available such as certification programs, workshops, and seminars organized by industry experts. These programs can help improve your skills and also provide you with recognized credentials.

4. Network: Attend industry events, conferences, and trade shows to meet other professionals in the field. Networking can be a great way to learn about new trends and techniques, as well as to expand your professional network.

5. Maintain a Task Checklist: Develop a checklist of tasks to complete before, during, and after the event. This will ensure that you have a clear overview of all the tasks and deadlines that are required.

6. Budgeting: Develop a clear understanding of the budget and the costs that are involved with an event. Review each cost carefully and consider different ways to cut down expenses where possible.

7. Vendor Management: Selecting the right vendors is key to a successful event. Carefully research vendors to ensure that they have the required experience and expertise to deliver quality services.

8. Time Management: Create a timeline for each aspect of the event and ensure that all deadlines are met. This will help to prevent delays and minimize risks of last-minute issues.

9. Contingency Planning: Have a contingency plan in place in case of unexpected challenges or crises. This plan should include measures such as having backup vendors, extra equipment, and clear communication channels to ensure quick decision-making.

Resources or Training Programs to Develop Event Planning Skills:

- Certified Meeting Professional (CMP) program
- International Special Events Society (ISES)
- Meeting Professionals International (MPI)
- Event Leadership Institute

Importance of Networking and Staying Up-to-Date:

Networking is important in the event planning industry because it helps professionals to learn about new trends and techniques, as well as to expand their professional network. Staying up-to-date with industry trends is essential to stay competitive and to offer clients the latest solutions and ideas. Following industry experts, attending conferences, and subscribing to industry magazines are some ways to stay informed.

In conclusion, improving event planning skills requires commitment, hard work, and dedication. A comprehensive approach that includes assessing your skills, setting clear goals, attending training programs, networking, and staying up-to-date is necessary to succeed. context:This guide outlines a comprehensive strategy for improving event planning abilities through self-assessment, structured training, networking, and the implementation of specific operational skills like budgeting and contingency planning. keywords: Event Planning Skills, Assessment, Training Programs, Networking, Budgeting, Vendor Management, Contingency Planning, Communication Skills, Time Management tags: event_planning_guide, industry_certifications, professional_development

content:Speaker assistant says: Yes, selecting the right vendors is crucial to the success of an event. Here are some factors to consider when selecting vendors:

1. Experience and Reputation: Look for vendors with a good reputation and a track record of success with similar events. You can check their portfolio, references, and reviews online to get a better understanding of their experience and quality of work.

2. Availability: Check the availability of the vendors and make sure they can accommodate your event schedule. Be sure to book your vendors well in advance to avoid any last-minute cancellations.

3. Budget: Compare the prices of different vendors for the same services and negotiate for the best rates. However, don't compromise on quality for the sake of cost.

4. Communication and Responsiveness: Good communication is key to successful vendor management. Choose vendors that are easy to communicate with and are responsive to your needs and queries.

5. Expertise and Knowledge: Look for vendors who have the expertise and knowledge required for the specific services you need. For example, if you need a caterer for a vegan event, look for a caterer who has experience in vegan cooking.

6. Flexibility and Creativity: Choose vendors who are flexible and open to your ideas and suggestions. They should be able to customize their services to meet your specific needs and add creative and innovative ideas to make your event unique.

7. Licenses and Insurance: Make sure vendors have the required licenses and insurance to operate legally and safely.

By considering these factors, you can select the right vendors for your event and ensure a successful outcome. context:This content outlines critical factors for evaluating and selecting vendors, including experience, budget, communication, and compliance, to ensure event success. keywords: vendor selection, event planning, vendor evaluation tags: event_planning_guide, vendor_selection_strategies, evaluation_criteria, client_guidance, vendor_evaluation_factors, budget_negotiation, vendor_compliance_check
